title: Loaded Nachos
subtitle: Oven-baked nachos with cheese, beans, and jalapeños
excerpt: Corn tortillas cut into triangles, baked until crisp, then loaded with melted cheese, spiced black beans, and jalapeños. Finished with soured cream and fresh coriander.

recipe.sourceNotes: Nachos were invented in 1943 by Ignacio Anaya Garcia in Piedras Negras, Mexico, who improvised a quick snack for a group of US military wives using the ingredients he had available: fried tortilla chips, cheese, and jalapeños. The loaded version with beans, soured cream, and guacamole developed through Tex-Mex cuisine. Making the chips from corn tortillas takes an extra step but gives better flavour than shop-bought packets.

content.text: Bake the corn tortilla triangles until completely dry and crisp before adding the toppings. Any residual moisture makes them soften under the cheese. Layer the chips and cheese twice: one layer in the middle, one on top, so every chip gets some cheese.

items.preparation: thinly sliced, or from a jar

content.text: Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Toss the tortilla triangles with the oil and a pinch of salt. Spread in a single layer on baking trays. Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until crisp and just beginning to colour. Watch closely: they burn quickly.
Meanwhile, warm the black beans in a small pan with the cumin and a pinch of salt.

Transfer half the crisped tortilla triangles to a roasting tin. Scatter half the beans and half the cheese over the top. Add the remaining chips, beans, and cheese. Lay the jalapeño slices over the top.
Bake for 6 to 8 minutes until the cheese is completely melted. Spoon over the soured cream. Scatter with coriander. Serve with lime wedges immediately.
